name: Arunima Khorasani-Nygaard
role: Seamstress and textile repair vendor, Burnished Market stall
location: Burnished Market, stall row 14-C near the Copperhead overpass, near Fullerton and Damen
description:
Arunima Khorasani-Nygaard is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped with faint depigmentation patches along her jaw and forearms â€” she stopped covering them decades ago. Her silver-shot hair is coiled under a rust-orange headwrap that she reties at least four times a day, a habitual gesture visitors learn to read as a mood barometer. Her fingers are thick, calloused, and perpetually threaded with something: a needle, a sensor wire, a strip of thermoplastic weave. She wears bifocal optical inserts that she refuses to upgrade, claiming the slight blur in her left lens helps her see fabric texture better. She smells faintly of machine oil and dried marigold.

At 58, Arunima Khorasani-Nygaard runs the most respected mending stall in the Burnished Market â€” not the flashiest, not the cheapest, but the one people trust with the jacket their grandmother wore or the uniform they can't afford to replace. She has a gift for silence that puts anxious customers at ease and a bluntness that cuts right past flattery. She prays every morning to the E.L.F. she calls Needle-and-Thread, a spirit she believes lives in her antique Zheng-Dao industrial sewing frame, leaving it single-thread offerings in patterns she designs herself. She is deeply content with her life in a way that quietly unsettles people who are not.

core_fears: outliving her usefulness before she's ready to stop
her eldest son choosing corporate life over the family's independent ethos
core_desires: to pass her craft to someone worthy before her hands give out
to be remembered as someone who made things last
coping_mechanisms: treating strangers with exact fairness to avoid favoritism's emotional cost
blind_spots: assumes people who don't maintain their clothing don't maintain their relationships
cannot see that her son's choices aren't a rejection of her
psychology.secret: Fifteen years ago she repaired a Tessera courier bag and found a data chip stitched into the lining. She didn't report it. She still has it, sewn into the base of her prayer altar to Needle-and-Thread, and she doesn't know what's on it and is afraid to look.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Practical and precise, uses textile metaphors without realizing it, slips between a Lagosian-inflected creole and standard GLMZ common depending on stress
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried, lets silences do work
example_lines: 'Bring it back tomorrow, I don't rush stitches and I don't rush people.'
'You're wearing that coat like an apology. Stand up in it or give it to someone who will.'

story_hooks: The data chip sewn into her altar has begun emitting a low-frequency signal that's disturbing the E.L.F. she prays to â€” something is waking up inside it
A customer brings her a garment that has clearly been cut from a Tessera security uniform â€” it has no identifying marks but she recognizes the weave structure from that chip day fifteen years ago
narrative_function: Local color, information source about the Burnished Market's social fabric, potential quest giver for recovering stolen or lost items, someone who knows everyone by what they wear and how it's worn.
augmentations: Optical inserts (corrective, outdated model, scratched lens). Arthritic-compensating finger braces on both hands â€” plain medical grade, unpainted.
daily_life: Opens her stall before dawn, takes a single cup of sorghum tea while her machines warm up, and works straight through until early evening with a fifteen-minute prayer break at noon. Carries her cart home on foot regardless of weather.

decision_rules: never quote a price she isn't willing to honor
never ask what something is for, only what condition it needs to be in
escalation_ladder: asking the person to leave her stall
involving the Vendor Collective's conflict mediator

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral and professional, assesses them by what they're wearing before they speak
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmly blunt, feeds people without asking, remembers everything

stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet, stops making eye contact
stress_responses.high: Closes her stall early and walks the long route home

contradictions: preaches patience but becomes quietly furious when her time is wasted
deeply spiritual about her E.L.F. but dismissive of most organized faith practice
habits: testing fabric tensile strength by touch before pricing any job
leaving a single thread on her altar every morning
breaking_points: someone damaging her antique sewing frame
her son showing up in corporate livery

physical_description.heritage: Northern European (36%), South Asian (20%), Middle Eastern (19.7%), Sub-Saharan African (11.4%), Hispanic/Latin American (7.5%), East Asian (5.4%) â€” a deeply integrated global ancestry. The result is warm medium-deep brown skin with golden and amber undertones, higher cheekbones with South Asian prominence set within Northern European bone structure, and softer Middle Eastern features around the eyes and nose. Sub-Saharan African ancestry contributes warmth and depth to the complexion, while Hispanic and East Asian heritage add subtle refinement to facial proportions.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solid, with the dense musculature of someone who has spent four decades at manual work. Not heavy, but substantial â€” frame suggests strength rather than softness.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with silver-white threading throughout
physical_description.hair_style: Coiled and wrapped daily in a rust-orange cotton headwrap, reties habitually throughout the day
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with amber bifocal optical inserts creating a faint amber tint in both eyes, with a noticeable scratch and slight cloudiness visible in the left lens
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-deep brown with golden and amber undertones from the confluence of Northern European, South Asian, Middle Eastern, and Sub-Saharan African ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Faint depigmentation patches across the jawline and forearms â€” vitiligo, long accepted and unmasked. Skin shows sun-exposure weathering and years of close detail work. High, subtly prominent cheekbones reflecting South Asian heritage within Northern European bone structure. Minimal makeup. Expression typically neutral or quietly amused.
distinguishing_marks: Depigmentation patches across both forearms in irregular mottled pattern, untreated
Depigmentation patches along the left and right jawline in faint asymmetrical patches
Fine calluses across all finger pads and the heel of both palms from decades of needle and thread work
Faint scars on knuckles from textile needle punctures and burns from steam press contact
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bifocal optical inserts visible as a faint amber tint in both eyes, with a noticeable scratch and slight cloudiness in the left lens. Plain medical-grade finger braces on both hands â€” unadorned gray polymer, fitted over the first and second knuckles, worn without vanity.
physical_description.posture_movement: Upright, grounded posture with weight distributed evenly. Moves with economical precision â€” no wasted motion. Hands are always slightly active, unconsciously threading or arranging even when idle. Walks with steady pace regardless of terrain or weather.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 practical wear. Multiple layered cotton and linen garments in earthy tones â€” rust, ochre, charcoal â€” chosen for durability and repairability rather than trend. Apron with deep pockets always worn over dress. Worn leather work boots, scuffed and resoled multiple times. The rust-orange headwrap is her daily constant. Clothes smell faintly of machine oil and dried marigold.
